title: CRLR/210/2007 of ARVIND PRASAD JOSHI Vs STATE AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
 Criminal Revision No. 210 of 2007
Arvind Prasad Joshi ......... Revisionist
 versus
State of Uttarakhand and others .......... Respondents

Mr. R.P.Nautiyal, Senior Advocate, assisted by Ms. Sangeeta Bharadwaj,
Advocate, present for the revisionist.
Mr. P. S. Soun, learned AGA, present for the State of
Uttarakhand/respondent.
Ms. Sangeeta Miyan, Advocate, present for the private respondents.
with
Criminal Revision No. 224 of 2007
Smt. Kalpana Joshi and others ......... Revisionists
 versus
Arvind Prasad Joshi .......... Respondent

Ms. Sangeeta Miyan, Advocate, present for the revisionists.
Mr. R.P.Nautiyal, Senior Advocate, assisted by Ms. Sangeeta Bharadwaj
present for the respondent.

JUDGMENT
Hon'ble U.C. Dhyani, J. (Oral)
An application under Section 125 Cr.P.C. was
moved on behalf of the wife and two minor children for
grant of maintenance allowance against the husband (and

2
the father of minor children). The marriage of wife with the
opposite party/husband was admitted. The birth of minor
children (one minor daughter and one minor son) from their
wedlock was also admitted.
2. While one Criminal Revision has been moved
by the applicants for enhancement of maintenance
allowance, the other criminal revision has been filed for
setting aside the impugned order.
3. Learned Principal Judge, Family Court,
Dehradun, vide impugned judgment and order dated
25.08.2007, allowed the applications of the applicants
under Section 125 Cr.P.C. O.P. Arvind Joshi was directed
to pay a sum of Rs. 9,000/- per month to the applicants.
Such maintenance allowance was to be counted from the
date of filing of application under Section 125 Cr.P.C.
4. The first question which arises for consideration
is- whether the applicants are unable to maintain
themselves? Learned Principal Judge, Family Court has
appropriately dealt with the matter. Aspersions were cast
upon applicant no. 1 that she was living in adultery with her
younger brother, which was negatived by the Family Court,
who also found that the applicant no. 1 was subjected to
mental cruelty and she is, therefore, living separately from
her husband for sufficient cause. O.P.-husband moved an
application for restitution of conjugal rights under Section 9
of Hindu Marriage Act, in the Court of District Judge,
Uttarkashi, which suit was dismissed. Learned

3
District Judge found that the allegations made by the
husband against the wife were not substantiated and thereby
found no force in the suit filed under Section 9 of Hindu
Marriage Act. It is held on the basis of this discussion that
the applicant no. 1 is not living separately from her husband
without sufficient reason. In other words, she has valid
reasons for living separately from her husband.
5. The next question which arises for consideration
is- how much of the maintenance allowance the applicants
are entitled to? Whereas the wife stated that her husband
was getting a salary of Rs.20,000/- per month and she
demanded Rs.15,000/- for the maintenance of her minor
children alongwith her, it is the contention of learned
counsel for the husband that the applicants are not entitled
to maintenance allowance. The husband filed a certificate
(paper no. 82-Kha) to show that he was posted as Junior
Engineer in the Irrigation Department and his 'take-home'
salary was Rs. 13,782/- per month. His basic salary was Rs.
9,375/- and total perquisites were Rs. 20,090/-.
Approximate one third of salary was deducted. Whereas,
the husband was living separately in Uttarkashi, the wife
has to feed her along with her two minor children, who are
school going children. She has to spent money on their fees
along with books, stationery, uniform etc. In view of the
said salary structure and the liability on the wife, who has to
maintain two children, along with her, it is held that the
court below has appropriately apportioned the salary among
the applicants (wife, daughter and son) and opposite party-

4
husband, who must be earning more after the
implementation of recommendation of Sixth Pay
Commission Report. It will not be in the fitness of things
either to set-aside the impugned order or to direct the
husband to pay more to his wife and children. The court
below has taken a balanced approach by directing the
husband to pay Rs. 9,000/- per month to his wife and
children. There is no illegality in the impugned order.
6. Criminal Revision No. 210/2007, as also
Criminal Revision No. 224/2007 are therefore, dismissed.
7. Mr. R.P.Nautiyal, Senior Advocate, representing
the husband, made a prayer that the arrears of the
maintenance allowance be directed to be paid in
installments, to which Ms. Sangeeta Miyan, learned counsel
for the wife & children said that she has no objection, if the
arrears are directed to be paid in quarterly installments of
Rs. 50,000/- each. It is accordingly directed that the arrears
be paid in the quarterly installments of Rs. 50,000/- each.
The first installment be paid on or before 16.09.2013. The
last installment will comprise of the balance amount, after
three installments of Rs. 50,000/- each are paid to the wife
(and the children).
 (U.C.Dhyani,J.)
Dt. July 15, 2013
Kaushal
